**3B.4 Research Note**

Mixed, but weak on the implementation side. Srettha’s government made some formal, rights-forward moves in 2024, especially treaty ratification and public human-rights language. But the record also shows continued arbitrary detention, a custodial death, and unresolved impunity for major security-force abuses. I did not find strong evidence that he built durable, independent complaint or oversight systems that actually constrained politically protected actors.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Thailand ratifies disappearance convention, urges law on torture and enforced disappearance | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-05-16 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/icpped140524-2?page=5d5bd3da15e39c306002aaf9 | Thailand deposited ratification of the disappearance treaty and said the anti-torture / anti-disappearance law would be an important tool. This is the clearest formal systems-building evidence for due process and abuse prevention. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Positive | Prime Minister delivers statement at 3rd Summit for Democracy, highlighting Thailand’s commitment to democracy, rule of law, and human rights at home and abroad | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-03-20 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/summit-for-democracy-3-2?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c306000683e | Srettha publicly aligned his government with democracy, rule of law, and human rights. This supports intent to build lawful institutions, though it does not show successful enforcement or independent oversight. | 3B.4 |
| Positive | Joint Statement by the Prime Minister of the Kingdom of Thailand and the Prime Minister of New Zealand | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-04-17 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/js170424-2?menu=5d5bd3da15e39c306002aafa&page=5d5bd3da15e39c306002aaf9 | The joint statement emphasized democratic values, human rights, good governance, rule of law, and multilateralism. That is consistent with the creation of lawful complaint and oversight systems, but still only indirect evidence. | 3B.4 |
| Positive | Statement by Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs at the High-level Segment during the 55th Session of the Human Rights Council | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kingdom of Thailand | 2024-02-28 | https://www.mfa.go.th/en/content/statement-vfm-280224?cate=5d5bcb4e15e39c3060006848 | Thailand said it promotes human rights for all, humanitarian assistance to all in need, dialogue, reconciliation, and inclusive societies. This is rights-protective rhetoric, but not proof of functioning oversight institutions. | 3B.4 |
| Negative | Thailand: New Government Slow to Protect Rights | Human Rights Watch | 2024-01-11 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights | HRW said the new government was slow to protect rights and urged it to end politically motivated prosecutions and drop charges against peaceful protesters. That points to weak due-process protection in practice. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Thailand: Tragic death of detained activist must be ‘wake-up call’ | Amnesty International | 2024-05-14 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/thailand-tragic-death-of-detained-activist-must-be-wake-up-call/ | Amnesty said Netiporn Sanesangkhom had been held in arbitrary detention for peaceful protest and died in custody. That suggests complaint and oversight systems were not preventing abuse in detention. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Thailand: Investigate Detained Youth Activist’s Death | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-23 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/23/thailand-investigate-detained-youth-activists-death | HRW said hundreds of monarchy critics were in pretrial detention and called for a prompt, transparent investigation into the custodial death. The need for outside pressure indicates the state had not built credible independent review mechanisms. | 3B.4, 3B.1, 3B.2 |
| Negative | Thailand: Last-Ditch Effort for Tak Bai Massacre Justice | Human Rights Watch | 2024-05-01 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/01/thailand-last-ditch-effort-tak-bai-massacre-justice | HRW said successive Thai governments had failed to prosecute those responsible for the Tak Bai crackdown deaths and injuries. Continued impunity for politically sensitive security-force abuses is strong evidence against effective independent accountability. | 3B.4, 3B.2, 3B.1 |

**Assessment**
- Best-supported positive finding: Thailand under Srettha made formal legal and rhetorical commitments to anti-disappearance and human-rights norms.
- Best-supported negative finding: the government still faced serious gaps in practical due process, complaint handling, and independent investigation, especially where politically sensitive abuse was involved.
- Overall reading: partial formal systems-building, but weak evidence of effective oversight or accountability in practice.

**Search gap**
I did not find 2024 evidence showing Srettha created or substantially strengthened an actually independent inspectorate, ombudsman-style complaint body, police accountability unit, prison monitoring mechanism, or special prosecutor system that produced visible outcomes against protected actors.
